data.description:
ACCEPTED DEBT, taken knowingly at deploy time (operator ruling, Atin, 2026-08-11: "we're fine to use that key for the time being and then we'll clean it up. Just be sure that it's clear"). This ticket IS the clarity.

WHAT SHIPPED. The deployed Marquee Worker holds R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID / R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY set from CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID / CLOUDFLARE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in code/platform/.credentials/.env. That credential is the shared Stage 11 platform S3 key with **Account -> R2 -> Admin Read & Write**, i.e. account-wide.

WHY IT MATTERS. Marquee's whole job on that credential is accepting ANONYMOUS PUBLIC UPLOADS from a CFP form. The key it holds can read, overwrite and DELETE every other bucket in the Projects account — today that is acetate-releases (Acetate's production updater artifacts), c11-public-videos and stage11-expandedcinema. Blast radius crosses into two unrelated projects that have nothing to do with this conference.

IT ALSO CONTRADICTS AN EXISTING REQUIREMENT: MRQ-14's real-Cloudflare handoff explicitly asks to 'provision least-privilege S3 vars/secrets'. This is not new scope; it is an unpaid part of MRQ-14 carried by MRQ-57.

THE FIX (~10 minutes, needs the dashboard). R2 -> Manage API tokens -> Create token, Object Read & Write scoped to the marquee-media and marquee-media-preview buckets ONLY. Then: wrangler secret put R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID / R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY against the marquee Worker, redeploy, and re-run an upload end to end. No code change — the Worker reads both off env and does not care where they came from.

ALSO ROTATE-WORTHY WHILE HERE: MARQUEE_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (cfut_..., minted 2026-08-11, expires 2027-06-03) was pasted into a chat transcript at creation. Same house precedent as the keys.txt entries. Harmless for a demo; rotate before Marquee carries real conference data.
data.title: Replace the Marquee Worker's account-wide R2 key with a bucket-scoped credential

data.body: PLAN — isolated branch mrq-89-bucket-scoped-r2 cut from refreshed github/main at 1128629d9058. Will prove the account-token derivation with a real signed 200 before setting secrets; deployed upload plus foreign-bucket denial are required. API-token rotation remains deferred pending Atin.

data.reason: Current MARQUEE_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN returns 403/9109 for account token permission groups, so it cannot mint the R2 token. In Cloudflare R2 -> Account Details -> Manage API tokens -> Create Account API token, choose Object Read & Write and only marquee-media plus marquee-media-preview; do not paste the secret into chat. Resume this ticket once the one-time Access Key ID and Secret Access Key are available through the local secret workflow.

data.body: BLOCKER EVIDENCE — The current scoped MARQUEE_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN can access the Projects account and R2 buckets, but GET /accounts/{account_id}/tokens/permission_groups returned HTTP 403, Cloudflare error 9109 Unauthorized to access requested resource. It lacks Account API Tokens Write/Read, so the API mint path cannot be used with the supplied credential. Cloudflare's R2 docs confirm the derivation (Access Key ID = API token id; Secret Access Key = SHA-256 of token value), the bucket resource form, and Object Read & Write semantics, but live 200 proof is intentionally not claimed until Atin creates the token. Dashboard path: R2 -> Account Details -> Manage next to API Tokens -> Create Account API token -> Object Read & Write -> marquee-media and marquee-media-preview only. No Worker secrets, buckets, foreign-project objects, or deployment were changed.

SECURITY FOLLOW-UP — A complete R2 token value/access-key/secret pair was posted in chat. It has not been used, logged, or installed. Treat it as compromised: revoke it, mint a replacement with Object Read & Write on only marquee-media and marquee-media-preview, and provide it only through a local hidden prompt/secret workflow. Endpoint is non-secret and was not repeated.

data.note: Previous API-permission blocker superseded: a replacement credential is now required because the candidate pair was pasted into chat.

data.reason: Revoke the R2 token that was pasted into chat; it is compromised. Create a fresh Object Read & Write pair scoped only to marquee-media and marquee-media-preview, then enter it through a hidden local prompt/secret workflow rather than chat.

data.note: Operator explicitly overrode the demo credential risk and surface:290 is taking MRQ-89 to completion; no Worker secret or redeploy was performed here.

provenance.reason: Handed to surface:290 for completion; this agent performed no credential installation or deployment.

data.body: HANDOFF — Standing down per operator instruction. Surface:290 owns scoping proof, Worker secret installation, deployed upload validation, and closure. This agent did not push secrets or redeploy; the branch remains unmodified at the pre-deploy state.

RESTART CHECK — mrq-89-bucket-scoped-r2 is clean: no uncommitted files, no commits to push, and no Worker secrets or deployment actions were performed by agent:codex-cli. Its HEAD is 1128629 (MRQ-57 deploy) and it is behind the now-current github/main at cb0bc3c6 by five commits; any future resume must rebase from current github/main, not the stale branch. Surface:290 owns completion; prior comments contain the API 403/9109 blocker, exposed-pair caveat, and handoff.

MRQ-89 COMPLETE — bucket-scoped R2 credential is live on the deployed Worker.

**Credential.** Minted by Atin in the dashboard: Object Read & Write, scoped to
`marquee-media` + `marquee-media-preview` only. Stored as `MARQUEE_R2_*` in
`code/platform/.credentials/.env` (0600). The account-wide `CLOUDFLARE_R2_*` pair is
untouched — other projects still run on it.

**Scoping proven BEFORE install (6/6).** The point of this ticket is the denial, not the access:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| PUT + HEAD `marquee-media` | PASS |
| PUT `marquee-media-preview` | PASS |
| `acetate-releases` | **DENIED** |
| `c11-public-videos` | **DENIED** |
| `stage11-expandedcinema` | **DENIED** |

Read attempts only against the three foreign buckets — a least-privilege proof must never
itself become a write incident. Repeatable script: `scratchpad/validate-r2-scoping.sh`.

**Installed.** `wrangler secret put R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. No code
change, as the ticket predicted — the Worker reads both off `env`.

**End-to-end on the deployed build (1128629d9058)**, via an authenticated speaker session:

- `sign` → 200, presigned URL carrying `X-Amz-Credential=ff4d458c...` — the **new** key. This
  is the proof the deployed Worker actually picked up the rotation, rather than the weaker
  proof that a working key exists somewhere.
- `PUT` → 200 to R2
- `complete` → 200, `status: ready`
- media origin serves it 200 `image/png`; app host 404s the same path, so origin isolation holds.

A 1×1 probe was correctly rejected first with `dimension_too_small`, which incidentally proves
`complete` really reads the object back from R2 rather than trusting the client.

**Also rotated tonight** on the same Worker (separate from this ticket, same audit):
`RESEND_API_KEY` is now a Marquee-scoped send-only key locked to `stage11.systems`, and both
`UPLOAD_TOKEN_SECRET` and `UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT_SECRET` were rolled.

**Debt this ticket deliberately does NOT clear:**

1. This R2 pair was pasted into a chat transcript. Atin accepted that knowingly on demo
   grounds — twice, to `agent:codex-cli` on surface:289 and to me. **Rotate before Marquee
   carries real conference data.** The `.credentials/.env` entry carries that note inline, so
   the debt lives where the key lives rather than in a chat nobody re-reads.
2. `MARQUEE_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` has the same history and is still un-rolled.

**Residue:** one 512×512 probe headshot attached to seeded speaker `per_aarush-selvan`. Not
visible on the public speaker API. `reset:demo` would clear it; not run, because the fleet is live.

Bucket-scoped R2 credential installed and verified on the deployed Worker. Scoping proven before install: writes/reads its own two buckets, DENIED on acetate-releases, c11-public-videos and stage11-expandedcinema (read attempts only — 6/6). End-to-end on deployed build 1128629d9058: sign returned a presigned URL carrying the new access key id, PUT 200, complete 200 status ready, media origin serves 200, app host 404s the same path. Two debts left open and documented rather than silently closed: this pair was pasted into chat (Atin accepted knowingly for the demo — rotate before real conference data), and MARQUEE_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN has the same history and is still un-rolled. Full evidence in the review comment.

Completed by surface:290 against the DEPLOYED Worker. Merge-driver review of the evidence.

The credential was scope-proven BEFORE install, not after — writes and reads on marquee-media and marquee-media-preview, DENIED on acetate-releases, c11-public-videos and stage11-expandedcinema, 6/6. That ordering matters: proving least privilege after installing a key tells you what you already shipped rather than what you are about to.

The proof that convinces me is not that the new key exists but that the deployed Worker picked it up: the presigned URL came back carrying X-Amz-Credential=ff4d458c..., the new bucket-scoped key, on a live sign -> PUT -> complete -> status ready round trip, with the media origin serving 200 and the app host 404ing the same path. A rotation that is only proven by 'the secret was set' is not proven at all.

The read-attempt-only rule on the three foreign buckets was honoured — list-objects-v2 only, never a write. A least-privilege check that writes to prove it cannot write is itself the incident it was meant to prevent.

Blast radius closed: before this, the Marquee Worker — whose job is accepting ANONYMOUS PUBLIC uploads — held account-wide R2 admin credentials that could delete two unrelated projects' buckets. Also rotated on the live Worker in the same pass: RESEND_API_KEY (now Marquee-scoped, send-only, stage11.systems only) and both upload signing secrets.

RESIDUE, verified and deliberately left: the end-to-end test attached a real 512x512 gray probe headshot to seeded speaker per_aarush-selvan. I checked the public surface directly rather than taking it on trust — the speakers embed renders zero img elements, so no headshot is visible to a judge on any public page. Ruling: LEAVE IT. reset:demo is destructive, would land on a live deployment mid-fleet, and trades a verified 9958-row seed for the removal of something nobody can see. If it is to go, it goes as part of a deliberate pre-recording reset, not as cleanup.
